crop.notes: Whole item, headline to closing rule, top of the far-right column of the sporting page.

ocr.notes: Small errors: 'Charlie Day' should be 'Charlie Daly'; 'who knew Allen' drops 'well'; 'boxing bouts' drops 'and feats of strength'; 'hope to have' should be 'hope to arrange to have'; 'Park Hall' should be 'Lemp's Park Hall'.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Allen's friends, led by R. W. L. Gillespie and his pallbearers, planned a boxing benefit to buy a monument for his grave in Calvary Cemetery, saying he left no estate.

metadata.notes: Masthead: Saturday, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, April 11, 1903 (sporting page).

facts.fact: Allen was buried in Calvary Cemetery, St. Louis, on Wednesday after his death
Allen's pallbearers were Charlie Daly, Chris Lauff, Jack Fletcher, Tom Kelly, T. Neusel, Tom O'Donnell and Gus Ellis
Friends led by R. W. L. Gillespie planned a benefit of boxing bouts, probably at the West End Club, to pay for a monument and care of Allen's grave, Gillespie saying Allen left no estate

notes: Burial place given as Calvary Cemetery here; the Post-Dispatch of the next day (209) says Bellefontaine Cemetery. The facts index lists both.
